items.title: Same Class, Different Risk? Dapagliflozin versus Empagliflozin and Genitourinary Safety in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are guideline-directed therapy for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but comparative genitourinary safety data for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in HFpEF-treated populations remain limited. To compare 6-month symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI), asymptomatic bacteriuria, and other genitourinary adverse events among patients newly initiated on dapagliflozin or empagliflozin for HFpEF. This retrospective, single-centre comparative cohort study included 239 adults with physician-documented HFpEF retained after a requirement for at least 6 months of continuous follow-up: 113 received dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily and 126 received empagliflozin 10 mg once daily. The original outcome of any documented bacteriuria/UTI was separated into symptomatic UTI and asymptomatic bacteriuria. Risk differences and 95% confidence intervals were calculated; a multivariable logistic model of the original documented bacteriuria/UTI composite adjusted for age, sex, and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Any documented bacteriuria/UTI occurred in 21/113 (18.6%) dapagliflozin-treated participants and 25/126 (19.8%) empagliflozin-treated participants. Symptomatic UTI occurred in 4/113 (3.5%) and 5/126 (4.0%), respectively; 17/113 (15.0%) and 20/126 (15.9%) had documented asymptomatic bacteriuria. The risk difference for the composite, calculated as empagliflozin minus dapagliflozin, was 1.3 percentage points (95% CI -8.9 to 11.2). The adjusted odds ratio was 1.62 (95% CI 0.76-3.45; p = 0.208). Other genitourinary events were uncommon and estimates were imprecise. No statistically detectable between-group difference was found in symptomatic UTI, asymptomatic bacteriuria, or the original composite outcome. Confidence intervals were wide and compatible with clinically meaningful differences in either direction. These exploratory findings require confirmation in prospective multicentre studies with standardized culture ascertainment and complete follow-up. Inhibitorii cotransportorului sodiu-glucoză de tip 2 (SGLT2) reprezintă o terapie recomandată de ghidurile de practică clinică pentru insuficiența cardiacă cu fracție de ejecție păstrată (HFpEF), însă datele comparative privind siguranța genitourinară a dapagliflozinei și empagliflozinei la pacienții tratați pentru HFpEF rămân limitate. Compararea incidenței infecțiilor simptomatice de tract urinar (ITU), a bacteriuriei asimptomatice și a altor evenimente adverse genitourinare pe parcursul a 6 luni, la pacienții care au inițiat tratament cu dapagliflozină sau empagliflozină pentru HFpEF. Acest studiu retrospectiv, unicentric, de cohortă comparativă, a inclus 239 de adulți cu diagnostic de HFpEF documentat de medic, care au îndeplinit criteriul unei perioade de urmărire continuă de cel puțin 6 luni: 113 au primit dapagliflozină 10 mg o dată pe zi, iar 126 au primit empagliflozină 10 mg o dată pe zi. Criteriul de evaluare inițial, reprezentat de orice episod documentat de bacteriurie/ITU, a fost separat în ITU simptomatică și bacteriurie asimptomatică. Au fost calculate diferențele absolute de risc și intervalele de încredere de 95%. Pentru criteriul de evaluare compozit inițial, bacteriurie/ITU documentată, a fost utilizat un model de regresie logistică multivariată, ajustat pentru vârstă, sex și rata estimată a filtrării glomerulare (eGFR) la momentul inițial. Orice episod documentat de bacteriurie/ITU a fost identificat la 21/113 pacienți (18,6%) tratați cu dapagliflozină și la 25/126 pacienți (19,8%) tratați cu empagliflozină. ITU simptomatică a fost înregistrată la 4/113 pacienți (3,5%), respectiv 5/126 pacienți (4,0%), iar bacteriuria asimptomatică a fost documentată la 17/113 (15,0%), respectiv 20/126 (15,9%). Diferența absolută de risc pentru criteriul de evaluare compozit, calculată ca empagliflozină minus dapagliflozină, a fost de 1,3 puncte procentuale (IC 95%: −8,9 până la 11,2). Raportul cotelor (OR) ajustat a fost de 1,62 (IC 95%: 0,76–3,45; p = 0,208). Celelalte evenimente adverse genitourinare au fost rare, iar estimările au avut o precizie redusă. Nu au fost identificate diferențe semnificative statistic între cele două grupuri în ceea ce privește ITU simptomatică, bacteriuria asimptomatică sau criteriul de evaluare compozit inițial. Intervalele de încredere au fost largi și compatibile cu diferențe potențial relevante clinic în ambele direcții. Aceste rezultate exploratorii necesită confirmare prin studii prospective, multicentrice, cu evaluare microbiologică standardizată prin urocultură și urmărire completă a pacienților.

items.title: Genetic Insights Into Cardiomyopathy With Restrictive Phenotype: Implications for Diagnosis and Personalized Care.
items.abstract: Cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype is uncommon, genetically heterogeneous, and difficult to distinguish from advanced hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy. We aimed primarily to determine the diagnostic yield and spectrum of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants among patients with an echocardiographically defined restrictive phenotype; genotype-imaging and survival comparisons were prespecified exploratory analyses. We screened 568 patients with cardiomyopathy who underwent whole-exome sequencing and comprehensive echocardiography. Thirty-three met the operational definition of restrictive phenotype. Variants were classified. Genotype-imaging associations and survival were analyzed exploratorily. Among the 568 patients, 33 exhibited a restrictive phenotype: 7 had restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), 20 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HRCM), and 6 had dilated cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HDRCM). Variant carriers had a smaller aortic sinus diameter. In addition, MYBPC3 variant carriers had greater ventricular wall thickness and more frequent septal hypertrophy. Both the HRCM and HDRCM groups showed hypertrophic features, with interventricular septal hypertrophy occurring more frequently in the HDRCM group. The estimated 5-year survival was 54.5%, and survival did not differ significantly according to genetic-variant status. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were frequent in this single-center cohort with restrictive physiology and were associated with selected imaging features. These exploratory findings support integrated genetic and echocardiographic evaluation.

items.title: Cerebral Safety of Two Pulsed Field Ablation Workflows for Pulmonary Vein Isolation: Results From the Randomized TWOSOME MRI Study.
items.abstract: Data on silent cerebral events/lesions (SCE/SCL) following pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) are limited. This study aimed to assess the incidence of SCE/SCL using cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI) in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients undergoing PVI with two distinct PFA systems and workflows. In this prospective, single-center TWOSOME MRI substudy, patients with paroxysmal AF were randomized 1:1 to single-shot or single-tip PFA. Single-shot PVI was performed using a pentaspline PFA catheter (single-transseptal access, PV-angiography, no 3D mapping) and single-tip PVI using a PFA generator with a focal ablation catheter (double-transseptal access, 3D mapping). A predefined consecutive cohort underwent 1.5-T cMRI 24 h after the procedure. SCE were defined as acute cMRI-detected lesions resolving on 6-week follow-up cMRI, and SCL as persistent lesions. Baseline characteristics, neurological symptoms, procedural data, and cMRI findings were assessed. Fifty patients underwent cMRI (25 per group). Acute SCE were detected in 3/50 patients (6%; 95% CI 1.3-16.5), with 1/25 (4%) in the single-shot group and 2/25 (8%) in the single-tip group (p = 1.00). All SCE resolved on follow-up imaging, with no evidence of persistent SCL. One symptomatic stroke occurred in the single-shot group, unrelated to PFA, and was attributed to air embolization during transseptal puncture. No permanent neurological deficits occurred. In this exploratory cMRI study, both PFA workflows showed a low incidence of SCE without evidence of SCL or PFA-related neurological complications. Larger studies are required to compare cerebral safety profiles of PFA technologies. NCT07175727 (clinicaltrials.gov).

items.title: Preprocedural Computed Tomography Guidance Improves Accuracy of Right Ventricular Septal Lead Placement in Pacemaker Implantation.
items.abstract: Accurate right ventricular septal lead placement is crucial for optimal pacemaker performance and procedural safety, yet conventional fluoroscopy-guided implantation is limited by inter-individual anatomical variability. We therefore examined whether preprocedural computed tomography (CT) can provide patient-specific anatomical guidance to enable precise lead positioning. We retrospectively analyzed 501 consecutive patients who underwent initial dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for bradycardia pacing (non-CT-guided, n = 243; CT-guided, n = 258). In the CT-guided group, the midseptal target was determined preoperatively using multiplanar reconstruction of CT images, and reference lines were projected onto the scout image to guide lead placement. We evaluated the total procedure time, fluoroscopy time, right ventricular lead electrical parameters, implantation site, and complications. CT guidance was associated with a higher rate of septal lead placement than non-CT guidance (93.0% vs. 55.6%, p < 0.001), whereas free-wall lead placement was less frequent (7.0% vs. 44.4%, p < 0.001). The procedural radiation dose was lower with CT guidance (CT-guided, 100.2 ± 124.6 mGy vs. non-CT-guided, 169.1 ± 152.4 mGy; p < 0.001). Among patients with complete atrioventricular block and available postoperative paced QRS measurements (n = 303), QRS duration was shorter in the CT-guided group than in the non-CT-guided group (145.3 ± 22.3 ms [n = 165] vs. 155.4 ± 19.0 ms [n = 138], p < 0.001). The association persisted after multivariable adjustment ((adjusted OR, 10.30; 95% CI, 5.91-17.97; p < 0.001). The total procedure time, fluoroscopy time, and pacing parameters were comparable between the groups. Complication rates were low overall, and pocket hematoma was less frequent in the CT-guided group (0.4% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.03). Preprocedural CT guidance facilitated precise planning of the right ventricular lead target using scout images and was associated with accurate and reproducible placement at the intended septal site without prolonging procedural time or compromising electrical performance. This approach may represent a practical strategy for optimizing lead placement in bradycardia pacing.

items.title: Artifactual Contact Force Rise During High-Power Radiofrequency Delivery With the QDOT MICRO Catheter: A Comparative Study Using Non-Contact Tests.
items.abstract: Contact force (CF)-sensing technology ensures effective lesion formation and safety during radiofrequency (RF) ablation; however, the potential for an artifactual rise in CF, a false elevation not attributed to physical contact, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the occurrence and magnitude of artifactual CF rise between the QDOT MICRO catheter (QMc) and the Thermocool SmartTouch SF catheter (STSFc) using a non-contact RF delivery (NCRD) test. We retrospectively analyzed 135 patients who underwent NCRD testing in the right atrium (QMc, n = 93; STSFc, n = 42). The NCRD test was performed in a blood pool without tissue contact at power settings of 90, 50, and 40 W for QMc and 50 and 40 W for STSFc. The magnitude and incidence of CF rise (≥ 5 and ≥ 10 g) were compared. In the QMc group, a significant power-dependent increase in CF was observed: 9 g (IQR: 5-12 g) at 90 W, 3 g (IQR: 1-10 g) at 50 W, and 2 g (IQR: 1-3 g) at 40 W (p < 0.001). At 90 W, the incidence of CF rise ≥ 5 g was 76%, and that of CF rise ≥ 10 g was 46%, significantly higher than at lower settings. In contrast, the STSFc group exhibited stable CF measurements with no instances of CF rise ≥ 5 g. QMc also showed significant power-dependent elevation in electrode temperature. QMc exhibited significant power-dependent artifactual CF rise. These findings suggest that catheter-specific design and thermal effects may influence CF stability during RF delivery. Preprocedural NCRD tests may help identify catheter-specific CF instability before CF-guided ablation.

items.title: Chemical Modulation of the cGAS-STING-ENPP1 Axis: Medicinal Chemistry and Clinical Perspective.
items.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway plays a fundamental role in innate immune signaling and has emerged as a therapeutically relevant pathway across cancer, inflammatory, and autoimmune diseases. Herein, we provide a comprehensive medicinal chemistry-focused overview of both activation and inhibition of the cGAS-STING pathway, focusing on three druggable therapeutic targets, cGAS, STING, and ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1 (ENPP1). The translational maturity of these targets differs substantially, with STING being the most clinically advanced, whereas cGAS and ENPP1 remain emerging targets supported predominantly by preclinical evidence, with the advancement of a few inhibitors into early-stage clinical trials. The biological rationale for pathway modulation, along with modulators, is discussed with emphasis on active site interactions, scaffold diversity, their activity profiles, structure-activity relationships, species selectivity, and in vivo efficacy. The particular focus is on patent literature and advanced-stage molecules, discussing their ADME properties, pharmacokinetics, and clinical development status. Although STING agonists have achieved a larger reach in clinical trials within this pathway, recent developments suggest that cGAS inhibitors and ENPP1 inhibitors hold a greater promise for future clinical success. In summary, this review provides insights into medicinal chemistry and translational challenges and future opportunities for rational drug design to guide next-generation modulators of the cGAS-STING-ENPP1 axis.

items.title: Peripheral immune tolerance as a driver of tumor immune escape and therapy resistance.
items.abstract: Peripheral immune tolerance, essential for preventing autoimmunity, is increasingly co-opted by tumors to drive progression, metastatic dissemination, and immunotherapy resistance. Whereas central tolerance eliminates autoreactive clones, peripheral tolerance remains dynamically regulated by antigen persistence, cytokine gradients, metabolic cues, and stromal architecture, a plasticity that tumors exploit to build a multilayered immunosuppressive ecosystem. This narrative review synthesizes multi-omic, spatial, cellular, and molecular evidence, emphasizing 2021 to 2025 publications alongside foundational studies, to propose tumor-induced peripheral tolerance (TIPT) as a unifying framework for immune escape and treatment failure. TIPT emerges from coordinated suppression by tumor-resident regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory B cells, M2-like macrophages, tolerogenic dendritic cells, and exhausted CD8? T cells, sustained by suppressive cytokine networks, metabolic deprivation, epigenetic fixation of dysfunctional states, and stromal-vascular exclusion barriers. Spatially organized tolerance niches are associated with immune evasion, metastatic seeding, and resistance to checkpoint blockade. Strategies targeting suppressive cell populations, metabolic pathways, chromatin regulators, and stromal barriers are in clinical development, but clinical benefit has been established for only a limited subset, and anti-TIGIT antibodies failed to meet primary endpoints in phase 3 lung cancer trials. Machine-learning models show promise for predicting tolerance states and guiding combination design, but prospective clinical validation is still needed. TIPT may represent an important, potentially actionable determinant of tumor evolution and immunotherapy response, and durable cancer control is likely to require combined strategies that dismantle this tolerance ecosystem.
items.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico

items.title: Prognostic associations between patient-reported outcomes and progression-free and overall survival in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%: results from the RATIONALE-305 trial.
items.abstract: In RATIONALE-305, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival (OS) versus placebo plus chemotherapy in advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC) with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor area positivity (TAP) score ≥ 5% and in all patients. Here, we present a three-component joint model (JM) developed to evaluate associations between patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and risk of progression-free survival (PFS) and OS events. Longitudinal PRO data were analyzed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22. The JM linked: (1) a linear mixed model (LMM) for change from baseline in PRO scores; (2) a Cox model for time to recurrent symptomatic deterioration (RS-D); and (3) a Cox model to evaluate the RS-D event frailty prediction of PFS and OS. 475 patients in the PD-L1 ≥ 5% subgroup (tislelizumab + chemotherapy, n = 238; placebo + chemotherapy, n = 237) were evaluated. In PFS and OS LMMs, tislelizumab + chemotherapy versus placebo + chemotherapy was associated with improved GHS/QoL (global health status/quality of life) (p = 0.01) and reduced dietary restrictions (p = 0.05). In the OS LMM, tislelizumab + chemotherapy was associated with reduced upper GI symptoms (p = 0.01) and reductions in dietary restrictions (p = 0.02). RS-D in GHS/QoL, pain, and dietary restrictions were leading predictors of PFS risk. Across all QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22 domains, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly reduced the risk of progression or death (PFS HRs 0.55-0.65; 35-45% reduction) and death (OS HRs 0.65-0.73; 27-35% reduction); all p ≤ 0.01. PROs have significant prognostic value for disease progression and survival in patients with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%. NCT03777657 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov ). Stomach and gastroesophageal junction cancers are among the most common and deadly cancers worldwide, and patients often suffer significant symptoms that reduce their quality of life. While patient-reported outcomes (i.e., surveys where patients describe their own symptoms and wellbeing) are known to matter in cancer care, it has been unclear how changes in these reports over time relate to disease progression and survival. This study linked patients’ ongoing symptom reports with their clinical outcomes in a large clinical trial of the immunotherapy tislelizumab combined with chemotherapy. The results demonstrated that worsening health-related quality of life, pain, and dietary difficulties were early warning signs of disease progression or death, while treatment with tislelizumab consistently protected against both. These findings support using patient-reported disease-specific symptoms as meaningful clinical tools to guide treatment decisions and improve care for patients with advanced gastric cancer.
items.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

items.title: Distribution of Donor Types and Time to Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation for Acute Myeloid Leukemia Across Ethnic Groups: A Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: Identifying suitable donors and optimizing transplant timing are critical in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia. This retrospective study evaluated 124 Israeli adult AML patients (99 Jews, 25 Arabs) who underwent their first allo-HSCT between 2012 and 2022. We assessed donor types, key transplantation time intervals, overall survival, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Overall, 80.7% of patients received fully matched grafts. Donor type distribution differed significantly between ethnic groups (p = 0.007): Israeli Arabs predominantly received matched related donors (64%) with few matched unrelated donors (8%), whereas Israeli Jews showed a balanced distribution (41.4% each). Despite these differences, there were no significant disparities in time from diagnosis to transplantation (119 vs. 122 days, p = 0.871) or in overall survival. The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with prolonged time from coordinator referral to transplantation (p < 0.001) but did not significantly affect overall survival (p = 0.059). In conclusion, differences in donor type by ethnicity did not translate into disparities in transplantation timing or overall survival. These findings highlight the resilience of the transplantation process and the importance of evaluating ethnicity within the context of a specific healthcare system.

items.title: Machine learning-derived intracellular protein-based prognostic model reflecting a senescence-associated secretory phenotype-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related genes with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and clinical outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and to develop and evaluate a prognostic signature for risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was conducted to identify distinct molecular subtypes. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Random Forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were utilized to identify core prognostic SASP genes. The expression patterns of selected SASP-related genes were explored using multi-omics datasets, LUAD cell lines, and clinical specimens. Cluster 1 was associated with significantly shorter overall survival (OS), enhanced senescence pathway activity, and computationally inferred immunosuppressive and immune-exclusion features. Five intracellular SASP regulators- ANGPTL4 , CDKN2A , H2AX , MMP1 , and CCL20 -were selected through machine learning to construct the SASP Protein Regulator Score (SASP-PRS). A high SASP-PRS was associated with the activation of senescence/SASP and cell-cycle pathways, suppression of antitumor immune signatures, and distinct immune-checkpoint and chemokine expression profiles. A higher SASP-PRS was also associated with advanced disease stage, poorer OS, predicted lower responsiveness to immunotherapy, lower predicted sensitivity to erlotinib, and higher predicted sensitivity to selected chemotherapeutic agents. The nomogram incorporating the SASP-PRS demonstrated discriminatory ability and calibration for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS in the analyzed LUAD cohorts. These findings suggest that SASP-related gene-expression patterns are associated with LUAD molecular subtypes, senescence signaling, computationally inferred immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. The SASP-PRS may serve as a potential biomarker for prognostic stratification in LUAD. However, its utility for treatment-response assessment remains exploratory. Prospective external validation and functional studies are required to establish its clinical applicability and clarify the mechanisms linking SASP-related networks to the LUAD immune microenvironment.

items.title: Androgen receptor signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of male predominance and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is two to four times more common in men than in women. The sex distribution of viral hepatitis, alcohol use and adiposity explains only part of this difference, which points to sex-specific host biology as a further driver. The androgen receptor (AR), a ligand-activated transcription factor expressed in hepatocytes and in most HCC, is a strong candidate: both epidemiologic and experimental data implicate it in the male excess. This review draws that evidence together. Prospective cohorts link higher circulating testosterone and sex hormone-binding globulin to liver cancer risk, although raising SHBG experimentally suppresses rather than promotes hepatocarcinogenesis, a discordance that bears on how those associations should be read, and experimental studies group the underlying biology into several modules: constitutively active AR and its splice variants, kinase-driven phosphorylation of the receptor, downstream effectors of proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis, non-coding RNA circuits, androgen-metabolizing enzymes and the systemic endocrine axis, and the effect of androgen on the tumor immune microenvironment. The weight of each module differs across hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related, hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related, metabolic dysfunction-associated and anabolic steroid-induced disease. Therapeutic work remains largely preclinical and has centered on AR antagonists combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitors or immune checkpoint blockade, on degraders aimed at AR splice variants, on proteolysis-targeting chimeras and nucleic-acid approaches that eliminate ligand-independent receptor states, and on enzyme inhibitors. Two problems still limit translation: AR appears oncogenic in most settings but tumor-suppressive in some, and androgen suppresses antitumor immunity in certain contexts while enhancing it in others. Clarifying when each holds is what will determine whether AR-directed therapy, already established in prostate cancer, can be extended to liver cancer.

items.title: HBV-Associated Immune Remodeling of TNFSF10 + Monocytes Through the LPAR3-GALNT4 Axis During Pregnancy.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes, and monocytes may contribute to immune dysregulation associated with HBV-related pregnancy complications. However, the underlying mechanisms by which HBV influences monocyte function during pregnancy complications remain poorly understood. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from HBV-infected and uninfected pregnant women were analyzed using flow cytometry. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed in anti-TNFSF10 antibody-blocked PBMCs and LPAR3-overexpressing THP-1 cells. LPAR3 was overexpressed in THP-1 cells, followed by cell adhesion, migration, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence. Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from HBV-infected pregnant women revealed a significant reduction in TNFSF10 + monocytes compared with uninfected controls. Transcriptomic analysis of anti-TNFSF10 antibody-incubated PBMCs showed that LPAR3 was significantly upregulated in TNFSF10 + cells, with enrichment of pathways related to immune regulation and pregnancy-associated biological processes and innate immune responses. Hepatitis B virus X (HBx) overexpression impaired THP-1 cell adhesion and migration, and reduced TNFSF10 + monocyte-like characteristics, which were partially restored by LPAR3 overexpression. RNA-seq of LPAR3 overexpressing THP-1 cells revealed significant activation of immune and inflammatory signaling pathways. Furthermore, LPAR3 overexpression increased the expression of the glycosylation-related gene GALNT4, and GALNT4 restoration partially rescued HBx-induced impairment of monocyte adhesion and migration. LPAR3 may contribute to the regulation of monocyte functional states and TNFSF10 + monocyte-like characteristics, potentially contributing to immune dysregulation, highlighting LPAR3 as a potential target for immune monitoring and mechanistic exploration during HBV-associated pregnancy. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, and monocytes play a critical role in maternal immune regulation. However, the mechanisms by which HBV alters monocyte function and contributes to pregnancy complications remain unclear. This study identifies LPAR3 as a regulator of monocyte functional states and TNFSF10+ monocyte-like characteristics. HBV infection impairs monocyte adhesion and migration, which can be partially rescued by LPAR3 overexpression. LPAR3 may serve as a potential target for immune monitoring and mechanistic exploration in HBV-associated pregnancy, providing insights into immune dysregulation during maternal HBV infection.
items.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)

items.title: HEPATITIS C: THE PATH TO ELIMINATION.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is present in an estimated 4 million Americans in the United States. HCV prevalence rates are higher among persons experiencing homelessness and incarceration. Injection drug use is the most common mode of transmission in the United States, and new HCV infections have increased fourfold since 2005. Prior interferon-based treatment regimens offered low treatment rates and challenging side effects. Current HCV therapies with direct acting antivirals offer excellent response rates with minimal adverse events, and virologic cure leads to reductions in liver-related mortality. Despite therapeutic advances, many patients are not aware of their HCV infection. Even when diagnosed with HCV, rates of referral and antiviral treatment remain low. Our group has been studying efforts to improve rates of HCV testing and treatment.
items.journal: Transactions of the American Clinical and Climatological Association

items.title: Sex work or male-with-male sexual activity and the risks of HIV and hepatitis C acquisition among people who inject drugs: a global systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: People who inject drugs (PWID) may engage in sexual behaviours that increase their HIV and hepatitis C virus (HCV) risk, including sex work and male-with-male sexual activity. We undertook a global systematic review to assess whether PWID who engage in these behaviours have higher HIV and HCV acquisition risks. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO for studies among PWID published between 01/01/2000 and 09/06/2026 that included estimates of the association between male-with-male sex or sex work and our primary outcomes of HIV or HCV incidence. Studies that estimated incidence by longitudinally re-testing people at risk of infection or by using assays for recent infection were eligible for inclusion. We also contacted authors for unpublished estimates. We pooled estimates using random-effects meta-analysis. We used I 2 to assess heterogeneity, and we used Egger's test to assess publication asymmetry. This review is registered with Prospero (CRD42020220884). We included 57 studies comprising 164 estimates. Among men, recent male-with-male sex was associated with higher HIV acquisition (pooled incidence rate ratio (IRR):2.35; 95% CI: 1.51-3.66; I 2 : 51%).) but not HCV (IRR: 1.28; 95% CI: 0.95-1.72; I 2 : 21%). Recent sex work had a 1.72-fold (95% CI: 1.30-2.28; I 2 : 65%) and 1.59-fold (95% CI: 1.29-1.96; I 2 : 60%) higher HIV and HCV acquisition risk among all PWID, respectively. When stratified, sex work was associated with higher HIV acquisition among women (IRR: 2.30; 95% CI: 1.44-3.68; I 2 : 68%) but not men (IRR: 1.43; 95% CI: 0.92-2.22; I 2 : 51%), and was associated with HCV acquisition among men (IRR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.22-1.87; I 2 : 0%), but not women (IRR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.90-1.77; I 2 : 55%). For lifetime behaviours, only male-with-male sex was associated with HIV acquisition (IRR: 2.44; 95% CI: 1.18-5.02; I 2 = 87%). Results from Egger's tests did not provide evidence of asymmetry bias for our pooled estimates, while I 2 measures suggested considerable heterogeneity for many outcomes. PWID who also engage in sex work or male-with-male sex were found to have higher HIV or HCV acquisition risks. Future research should aim to understand the mechanisms driving these associations. Medical Research Council Greater Western Four Partnership Doctoral Training Partnership, Wellcome Trust, Canadian Institutes of Health Research and Medical Research Council.

items.title: Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess mimicking hepatic malignancy in a non-diabetic patient: A case report from Kazakhstan.
items.abstract: Pyogenic liver abscess is an infectious condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality, with Klebsiella pneumoniae emerging as a major pathogen. We report a case of Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess in a 76-year-old woman from Kazakhstan, representing one of the first indexed reports from Central Asia. The patient presented with prolonged fever, jaundice, and constitutional symptoms without diabetes mellitus. Initial ultrasound revealed a large heterogeneous hepatic mass with a solid, tumor-like appearance, raising concern for malignancy in the setting of chronic hepatitis B infection. MRI and contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated diffusion restriction, multiloculated architecture, and mild peripheral and septal enhancement without arterial hyperenhancement or venous washout, favoring hepatic abscess over hepatocellular carcinoma. The solid, tumor-like ultrasound appearance, atypical for a pyogenic abscess in its resemblance to hepatic malignancy, posed the primary diagnostic challenge, underscoring the value of multimodal imaging in characterizing hepatic lesions. Additionally, KPLA should be considered in the differential diagnosis even in the absence of classical metabolic risk factors and in regions with limited epidemiological data.

items.title: Regorafenib induces ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma via the EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling axis.
items.abstract: Regorafenib is a standard second-line multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor for sorafenib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Ferroptosis is a promising therapeutic cell-death modality, but the upstream signaling events governing regorafenib-induced ferroptosis remain unclear. We examined regorafenib activity in treatment-naive SNU-449 and HuH-7 HCC cells and mouse tumor models using ferroptosis-related assays, including reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), labile Fe 2+ , lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial ultrastructure. Transcriptome profiling was integrated with genetic and pharmacological modulation of EGFR and p65. Antitumor effects were assessed in HuH-7 xenografts and Hepa1-6 syngeneic tumors. Regorafenib suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth, with reduced Ki-67 expression. It downregulated SLC7A11/xCT and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and increased ROS, labile Fe 2+ , lipid peroxidation, and MDA; ferrostatin-1 partially restored viability and attenuated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptome analysis identified enrichment of the TNF signaling pathway. Regorafenib reduced total and phosphorylated EGFR and p65, decreased the p-EGFR/EGFR and p-p65/p65 ratios, and inhibited p65 nuclear translocation. p65 knockdown decreased SLC7A11/xCT and GPX4 and intensified ferroptosis, whereas p65 overexpression attenuated these effects. EGFR knockdown reduced TNF-α and enhanced ferroptosis; the EGFR agonist NSC228155 restored NF-κB activity and SLC7A11/xCT-GPX4 expression. Combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment further enhanced ferroptosis-associated phenotypes in vitro. Exploratory analysis of 24 paired specimens showed EGFR, p65, and GPX4 were upregulated and positively associated. These findings identify EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling as a functional upstream module in treatment-naive HCC models and support validating combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment in resistant models.

items.title: Negative-Pressure Fixation Improves RNA Preservation and Increases the Success Rate of the Oncomine Dx Target Test in Lung Cancer Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Samples.
items.abstract: Genetic tests for lung cancer, such as the Oncomine Dx Target Test (ODxTT), are essential for patient management, and require RNA and DNA of sufficient quality and quantity from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples. ODxTT fails due to poor nucleic acid preservation. Although enhancing the penetration of formalin into tissues improves nucleic acid preservation, the clinical utility of negative-pressure fixation methods remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated whether the negative-pressure fixation method using a vacuum fixation device improves ODxTT success rates and the quality of nucleic acids in FFPE samples from lung and other cancers, and examined the underlying mechanisms. The ODxTT success rate was higher with the negative-pressure fixation method than with the conventional method (96.5% vs. 81.2%), accompanied by increased RNA quality and yield; however, no marked differences were observed in DNA. RNA deteriorated more rapidly than DNA in resected mouse liver tissues, indicating that RNA is more labile than DNA during cold ischemia. Furthermore, in FFPE samples from colon, pancreatic, and prostate cancers, negative-pressure fixation consistently improved RNA DV200. These results indicate that the negative-pressure fixation method improves ODxTT success by accelerating formalin penetration, which may suppress RNase-mediated RNA degradation and preserve RNA quality.

items.title: Morpholino-mediated splice switching of NELFE suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell phenotypes in vitro and in vivo .
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is among the deadliest cancers worldwide, with rising incidence and few targeted therapies, driving high rates of recurrence and poor survival. Negative elongation factor E (NELFE), an RNA-binding subunit of the NELF complex, acts oncogenically when overexpressed and is associated with worse prognosis in HCC, yet no therapies target it. Here, we identify a rare germline intronic variant in the NELFE locus, NM_002904.6:c.943-110C>T (rs79208225) that promotes skipping of NELFE exon 10 and identifies patients with a trend toward longer recurrence-free survival and lower NELFE expression in their tumors. Mechanistically, the variant reduces U2AF2 occupancy at intron 9, likely through an indirect effect on splice-site recognition rather than direct disruption of U2AF2 binding. Recognizing exon 10 as a targetable splice event, we designed morpholino (MO) antisense oligonucleotides against its splice junctions that phenocopied the variant, lowering NELFE protein expression and impairing malignant phenotypes across HCC cell lines spanning diverse etiologies and NELFE expression levels. Delivered by ultrasound-targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD) in orthotopic liver tumors, NELFE MOs significantly reduced tumor burden and extended survival. These findings establish a naturally occurring splicing event as the basis for a localized, splice-switching therapeutic strategy for HCC.

items.title: Reciprocal MDK-THRB lipid-oxidation transcriptional programs in MASH-associated hepatocellular carcinoma: a two-cohort human transcriptomic analysis.
items.abstract: Midkine (MDK) and thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRB) have each been implicated separately in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). THRB drives hepatic fatty-acid beta-oxidation (FAO). We tested whether MDK and the THRB-linked FAO program are reciprocally related in human liver tissue. We analyzed two independent human cohorts on different platforms. TCGA-LIHC provided 374 tumor and 50 adjacent non-tumor RNA-seq samples. GSE164760 provided 53 NASH-HCC, 74 NASH, 29 non-tumoral NASH adjacent to HCC, 8 cirrhotic and 6 healthy microarray samples. We quantified MDK, THRB and a curated 21-gene hepatic FAO composite score. Tests included Mann-Whitney, Spearman, Kruskal-Wallis, Jonckheere-Terpstra and genome-wide correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. MDK was higher in tumor tissue in both cohorts (TCGA-LIHC p  = 1.0 × 10 -24 , GSE164760 p  = 8.1 × 10 -13 ). The FAO composite was correspondingly lower ( p  = 7.0 × 10-10 and p  = 7.1 × 10 -6 ). THRB itself was lower in GSE164760 ( p  = 3.9 × 10 -3 ) but not in TCGA-LIHC ( p  = 0.509). MDK correlated negatively with THRB and with the FAO composite in both cohorts. The strongest association was MDK versus FAO composite (rho=-0.45 in each cohort). Within-group analysis showed that the THRB to FAO composite correlation persisted in almost every subgroup. The MDK correlations weakened in three smaller subgroups. Across the five GSE164760 disease states, MDK, THRB and the FAO composite each differed significantly (Kruskal-Wallis p   -5 ) and each followed a significant monotonic trend (Jonckheere-Terpstra one-sided p  -3 ). A reciprocal MDK-high and FAO-low transcriptional signature is reproducible across two independent human cohorts and across the MASH-to-HCC spectrum. These human tissue data support THRB agonism as a candidate therapeutic rationale in MASH-HCC that warrants prospective validation. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05104-3.
